title: Soft-eviction grace windows for tier prioritization and fallback model hedging
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: During cross-region capacity pressure and tenant quota exhaustion, the current tier router performs abrupt hard demotions (immediate downgrade from paid to free lanes or model spillover) causing large latency spikes and a surge of retries. We need a graceful, tenant-centric prioritization policy that smooths degradations and favors paying customers while avoiding global thundering behavior.

Goal: Implement a soft-eviction + grace-window mechanism for plan tiers (free, paid, enterprise) that: 1) preserves low-latency fast paths for enterprise customers under pressure; 2) applies quota-aware admission control for paid plans with short staggered grace windows instead of instant demotion; 3) uses fallback model hedging (variant selection) with per-tenant cohesion so that model switches are gradual and observable; and 4) provides clear metrics and controls in the Console for ops and SRE to tune behavior without code changes.
proposal_summary:
Introduce a Tier Gatekeeper component in the admission plane that tracks per-tenant quota debt and recent success/latency signals. On capacity pressure or when a tenant exceeds quota, the gatekeeper issues soft-eviction windows: short (~30s-5m) probabilistic demotions where a percentage of requests are routed to fallback variants or lower-tier queues rather than fully switching all traffic. The policy supports exponential backoff on retries, tenant-weighted randomization to avoid synchronized retry storms, and fast-path pinning for enterprise SKUs. Configurable knobs surfaced in Console: grace_window_seconds, initial_soft_pct, soft_ramp_step, max_soft_pct, enterprise_pin_ttl.

Key behaviors: 
- Quota-aware admission: use tenant consumption + rolling minute tokens to compute a debt score.
- Soft eviction sampling: start with initial_soft_pct of requests demoted; increase in steps if errors/latency remain high.
- Pinning and stickiness: enterprise requests can be pinned to fast-path for a TTL where possible.
- Hedged fallback model variants: when demoted, select lower-cost model variant with KV-cache compatibility to reduce cold-start regressions.
- Observability: surface per-tenant soft_eviction_rate, fallback_variant_rate, and recovery_time metrics.
design_decisions: Use a lightweight in-memory per-tenant state in the admission plane backed by distributed changelog for recovery (minimize cross-network latencies).
Prefer probabilistic soft demotion over deterministic threshold flips to avoid global synchronized effects.
Fallback variants must be chosen only from compatible model families (same tokenizer/kv cache layout) to avoid long warmups.
Expose runtime knobs in Console feature flags and provide a safe default policy to start in conservative mode.
Keep enterprise pinning separate from soft eviction to ensure SLAs are preserved where contracted.
tasks: Spec and proto for Tier Gatekeeper admission API (Ethan)
Implement per-tenant debt scoring and sample-based soft eviction (backend) (Maya)
Fallback variant selection service and compatibility checks (Alejandro)
Console controls: toggle and sliders for grace windows and soft % (Design + Frontend)
E2E test harness: synthetic load + quota exhaustion scenarios (QA)
Instrumentation: metrics (Prometheus) and traces (Jaeger) for soft_eviction lifecycle (SRE)
Release rollout plan and canary in us-west-2 cluster (Infra/Oncall)
acceptance_criteria: Under a synthetic quota exhaustion test, at least 80% of enterprise requests remain on fast-path (pinned) throughout the window.
Soft eviction increments traffic demotion gradually; no single tenant flips 100% of requests instantly in canary runs.
Fallback variants chosen are KV-cache compatible and show <15% token cost reduction regression vs baseline in perf benchmark.
Metrics emitted: tenant.debt_score, tenant.soft_eviction_pct, tenant.fallback_variant_rate, tenant.recovery_time.
Console exposes knobs and a per-tenant timeline view for soft eviction events and provides one-click rollback to disable soft eviction globally.
